podcast.title: Early Bands (High School)
podcast.body: Before forming The Trews, Colin McDonald played in "not serious" punk and grunge bands with friends in high school while living in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia. His first band with a buddy from grade nine was called "One-eyed Trouser Snake," inspired by Monty Python's "Meaning of Life." "I started playing in like not serious like kind of punk and grunge bands in high school with my friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

podcast.title: Emotional Reaction to "Highway of Heroes"
podcast.body: Colin McDonald was deeply moved when he first played "Highway of Heroes," a song he co-wrote about Nikola Goddard. He "started to cry," an unusual reaction for him to his own work, recognizing the song's profound power. "I started to cry. And I never done that with anything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

podcast.title: Illness on Ace Frehley Tour
podcast.body: Colin McDonald suffered a severe bronchial infection before and during the first three weeks of a six-week US tour opening for Ace Frehley. This left him unable to sing his usual high, hard vocal parts, which was particularly challenging given the audience was primarily "die-hard Kiss fans." He eventually recovered his voice after getting antibiotics in the US. "for the first like three weeks at Ace Freyly tour, I couldn't sing. It was a nightmare."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Formation and Early Cover Gigs (1996)
xref.body: The band started in 1996 in Colin McDonald's grandmother's basement, playing cover songs, including tracks by Tom Petty, The Beatles, The Tragically Hip, James Brown, and The Black Crowes. They gigged frequently in Antigonish high schools and local bars like Chuggles, Piper's Pub, and Pats Place, sometimes needing permission slips to play underage. "We started in 1996 and my grandmother's basement playing cover songs."

xref.title: Colin McDonald's Illness on Ace Frehley Tour
xref.body: Before a six-week US tour opening for Ace Frehley at House of Blues venues, Colin McDonald contracted a severe bronchial infection, losing his singing voice for the first three weeks. The audience, largely "die hard Kiss fans," were not typically receptive to new music. He eventually recovered his voice after obtaining antibiotics in America, leading Ace Frehley's famous sound engineer, Nightbob, to jokingly comment that he was "learning how to sing on this tour." "for the first like three weeks at Ace Freyly tour, I couldn't sing. It was a nightmare."

xref.title: Original Name: One-eyed Trouser Snake
xref.body: Before becoming The Trews, Colin McDonald had a punk/grunge band in high school in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia with a friend who shared a love for Monty Python. This earlier band was named One-eyed Trouser Snake, after a song from Monty Python's "Meaning of Life." When the core members (Colin, John Angus, Jack) formed, they adopted a shortened version, "One-eyed Trouser." "me and my buddy from grade nine really liked Monty Python and we called our first band One-eyed trouser snake from that song from Meaning of Life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Patreon Launch (Pandemic)
xref.body: At the beginning of the pandemic, The Trews launched a Patreon account. As part of this initiative, they distributed leftover copies of their rare 1997 "One-eyed Trouser EP," which had been stored at Colin McDonald's mother's house, to their "diehard fans." "We launched a Patreon at the beginning of the pandemic and one of the, and we had a bunch of these leftover trouser EPs from my mom's house and we gave them to a bunch of our diehard fans."

xref.title: Supportive Crew
xref.body: The crew working for Ace Frehley during his US tour with The Trews were noted for being "super accommodating and really sweet." This support was particularly appreciated by Colin McDonald, who was suffering from a severe bronchial infection at the time. "their crew was always really cool with us. They were super accommodating and really sweet."
